Lisa — thanks, we can definitely support the accelerated path. Attached is a first-draft MAP (aegis_map_v1.xlsx) and an evaluation plan outline. TL;DR on acceptance criteria we propose for the MAP so procurement can review quickly:

MAP acceptance thresholds (recommended):
- TTFT (cold prefix + KV warm): p50 < 150 ms, p95 < 650 ms, p99 < 1.6 s
- Streaming latency (first token after request): p50 < 220 ms, p95 < 580 ms, p99 < 1.3 s
- Sustained concurrency target: 64 concurrent chat sessions (80 token responses) with <10% tail latency degradation vs single-client baseline
- Throughput: >= 18k tokens/sec aggregate across the cluster at 64 concurrent sessions (measured at model output layer)

Evaluation plan summary:
1) Smoke run (2 hours): verify environment, model pull, network settings, tracing hooks.
2) Baseline runs (4 hours): single-client TTFT and streaming latency at several prompt/response sizes.
3) Concurrency sweep (24 hours): increment concurrency 8 -> 16 -> 32 -> 64 -> 96, 1-hour steady-state runs each, capture p50/p95/p99 and token/s.
4) Production pattern replay (12 hours): replay Aegis anonymized chat logs (sample provided) with KV cache patterns enabled.
5) Acceptance pass (4 hours): final run at target concurrency and final Grafana dashboards + automated artifacts.

We will provide: scripts (k6 + runc), a Docker image tag for the agent, and a CSV template for results. Proposed test window: 11/08 03:00 UTC -> 11/10 03:00 UTC.

I'll coordinate Marcus for the instrumentation and Connor for the deployment side. If that window doesn't work, tell us preferred dates.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Looping in preliminary numbers from an internal run that mirrors Aegis parameters. I've attached the raw CSV (streaming_ttft_results_20271104.csv). Key takeaways so far (single-cluster, 8x A100 equivalent nodes, model variant: redwood-14b-q4):

- TTFT (end-to-end, include tokenization): p50 = 132 ms, p95 = 490 ms, p99 = 1.18 s
- Streaming first-token latency (network + runtime): p50 = 210 ms, p95 = 510 ms, p99 = 1.05 s
- At 64 concurrent sessions (80 token responses) aggregate throughput measured: 19,300 tokens/sec
- 96 concurrent sessions showed increased tail: p95 TTFT rose to ~820 ms; streaming p95 ~980 ms.

Notes / items to run during Aegis window:
- Run with KV prefix caching enabled and disabled (we expect ~20–30% TTFT improvement with warm KV).
- Measure impact of batch size tuning: try batch targets of 8/16/32.
- Log GPU utilization + kernel-level timings (we'll ship a small hook for nsight metrics).

If Aegis agrees to the acceptance thresholds Mina proposed, we can schedule the 48–72h run. Otherwise we can adjust the MAP to stricter or looser targets.

On the attachments: CSV has per-run p50/p95/p99 and qps snapshots, plus a Grafana export.

—Marcus
